lead: A plain Turing machine has one tape and one head. Matching 0ⁿ1ⁿ then needs walking back and forth. Two variants remove that friction. A multitape machine has k tapes and k heads. A nondeterministic machine may choose among several moves at one step. Neither adds power: both accept exactly the recursively enumerable languages. They exist for shorter designs, faster algorithms and clean definitions of complexity classes.
prereq: You need: the model and instantaneous descriptions from 5.1 and acceptance from 5.2.

sections.h3: A multitape machine has k heads

blocks.text: A multitape Turing machine has k tapes and one head per tape. k is fixed when the machine is built; two or three tapes cover every design you will meet. Each tape is infinite to the right and holds symbols from Γ, which contains blank B. The input is on tape 1; other tapes start blank and serve as scratch. If a head at cell 0 is told to move left, it stays on cell 0.
δ: Q × Γ<sup>k</sup> → Q × Γ<sup>k</sup> × {L, R, S}<sup>k</sup>
blocks.where: Q is the finite state set; Γ is the tape alphabet; Γ<sup>k</sup> is the k-tuple of scanned symbols; {L, R, S} is the direction for each head — L left, R right, S stay.

blocks.text: One step reads state q and the k scanned symbols a₁ … a<sub>k</sub>. It writes a new symbol on each tape, moves each head, and enters a new state. This is one move, so copying between tapes is cheap.

items: 0ⁿ1ⁿ in one pass: copy zeros to tape 2, then erase one zero per 1.
A work tape keeps partial results while tape 1 is reread.
Extra tapes give bookkeeping, not power: three tapes accept no new language.

blocks.text: Nondeterministic: the next move is not unique. δ: Q × Γ → 2<sup>Q × Γ × {L, R, S}</sup>. Here 2<sup>S</sup> is the set of all subsets of S. The set may be empty, halting that branch, or contain several triples (q′, b, D).

A run is a path in a tree of configurations. A configuration is the full snapshot from 5.1: state, tape, head position. M accepts w if some run reaches q_accept. M rejects w only when every run halts without q_accept.
Use nondeterminism to “guess and verify”: guess the middle of a string, a maze path, or a factor. The check is deterministic work on the tape. Section 3 shows guesses cost time but add no languages.

sections.h3: Both variants accept the same languages

blocks.text: Theorem: single-tape, multitape and nondeterministic machines accept exactly the recursively enumerable languages. A single-tape machine is a special case. The other direction is a simulation.

items: Encode k tapes on one tape as T₁#T₂#…#T<sub>k</sub>.
Mark each head by a marked copy of the scanned symbol.
One move: sweep right to collect marks, decide, sweep again to write and shift marks.
After t steps the tapes use O(t) cells, so one sweep costs O(t) and the simulation costs O(t²).

blocks.text: For nondeterminism, simulate by breadth-first search of the configuration tree. Keep a queue of configurations on tape 2 and the current one on tape 3. If any branch accepts, the search finds it and M accepts. With b choices per move, depth t has at most 1 + b + b² + … + bt nodes, so the run is exponential in t. If every branch halts without accepting, the search empties its queue and M rejects. If some branch runs forever, the search never stops — allowed, because the language is only required to be recognised on the strings it contains, as in 5.2.

figure.caption: One finite control drives two heads, each scanning its own tape. Tape 1 carries 0011; tape 2 holds copied zeros. Heads move independently in one machine step.

spec.title: Two-tape Turing machine
spec.aria: One finite control drives two independent heads, each scanning its own tape.

examples.question: Design a two-tape Turing machine M that accepts L = {0ⁿ1ⁿ | n ≥ 1}. Give the transition function, trace the run on w = 0011, and state the final tape contents and number of moves.
steps: Q = {q0, q1, q_accept, q_reject}, Γ = {0, 1, B}, Σ = {0, 1}, start q0. Tape 1 holds 0011; tape 2 is blank.
Phase 1: δ(q0, 0, B) = (q0, 0, 0, R, R). Each 0 is copied to tape 2 and both heads move right.
End phase 1: δ(q0, 1, B) = (q1, 1, B, S, S).
Phase 2: δ(q1, 1, B) = (q1, 1, B, S, L); δ(q1, 1, 0) = (q1, 1, B, R, L). A 1 skips a blank on tape 2, or erases one 0 and moves head 1 right and head 2 left.
Halting: δ(q1, B, B) = (q_accept, B, B, S, S); δ(q1, B, 0) = (q_reject, B, 0, S, S); δ(q0, B, B) = (q_reject, B, B, S, S), rejecting the empty string.
Trace: moves 1–2 copy the two 0s. Tape 1 = 0 0 1 1, head 1 on cell 2 holding 1; tape 2 = 0 0 B, head 2 on cell 2 holding B.
Move 3: δ(q0, 1, B) = (q1, 1, B, S, S). Move 4: δ(q1, 1, B) = (q1, 1, B, S, L), head 2 to cell 1 holding 0.

Move 5: δ(q1, 1, 0) = (q1, 1, B, R, L). Tape 2 = 0 B B; head 1 on cell 3; head 2 on cell 0. Move 6: same rule. Tape 2 = B B B; head 1 on cell 4 holding B; head 2 stays on cell 0, now B, by the convention in Section 1.
Move 7: δ(q1, B, B) = (q_accept, B, B, S, S).
examples.answer: M accepts 0011. Tape 1 is unchanged 0011; tape 2 has no zeros. The run takes 2n + 3 = 7 moves, and 2n + 3 for every 0ⁿ1ⁿ with n ≥ 1. On strings with more 1s than 0s, e.g. 011, M never halts (head 2 moves left while head 1 stays on a 1), so M recognises L but does not decide it.

w = "0011"
n = w.count("0")
print(len(w))
print(n)
print(w.count("1"))
tape2 = ["0"] * n
for i in range(n):
    tape2[i] = "B"
print(sum(1 for c in tape2 if c == "0"))
print(2 * n + 3)

traps: Variants add no power. Every language is still recursively enumerable.
O(t²) is the single-tape simulation cost over t multitape moves; the multitape machine itself runs in t.
Nondeterministic acceptance needs one accepting branch. Rejection needs all branches to fail, so the simulation may run forever on rejected strings.
k tapes mean k heads. One head cannot read all tapes at once, and heads need not move together.
An empty δ set is a dead end for that branch, not a syntax error.

quiz.q: Write the transition signature of a k-tape Turing machine and name each part.
quiz.a: δ: Q × Γ<sup>k</sup> → Q × Γ<sup>k</sup> × {L, R, S}<sup>k</sup>. Q is the state set, Γ the tape alphabet, Γ<sup>k</sup> the k scanned symbols, and the last part gives one direction per head.

quiz.q: What does δ(q, a) return for a nondeterministic Turing machine?
quiz.a: A finite set of triples (q′, b, D) from Q × Γ × {L, R, S}. The set may be empty, which halts the branch.

quiz.q: Why do extra tapes not increase the set of accepted languages?
quiz.a: The k tapes can be written on one tape with separators # and head positions marked with dotted symbols. One multitape move becomes two sweeps of a single tape, so a single-tape machine can imitate every run.

quiz.q: Run the two-tape machine of the worked example on w = 000111. How many 0s are on tape 2 after phase 1, and how many moves does the whole run take?
quiz.a: n = 3, so tape 2 holds three 0s after phase 1. The run takes 2n + 3 = 2 × 3 + 3 = 9 moves, ending in q_accept with tape 2 empty.

quiz.q: A multitape machine runs for t = 1000 moves. Give the order of the number of single-tape moves the O(t²) simulation needs.
quiz.a: About t² = 1000 × 1000 = 10⁶ cell visits, up to a constant factor from the two sweeps per simulated move.

quiz.q: Why is the single-tape simulation O(t²) and not O(t)?
quiz.a: After t simulated moves the used part of the single tape has length O(t). Each simulated move sweeps that whole region twice, once to read the marked symbols and once to write them, so the total is O(t) × O(t) = O(t²).

quiz.q: The deterministic breadth-first simulation of a nondeterministic machine may never halt on some input. Does that break the equivalence of the two models?
quiz.a: No. The languages are recursively enumerable, not necessarily recursive. The simulation must halt and accept whenever some branch accepts; on an input with no accepting branch it may loop forever, which the definition of acceptance permits.

beyond: Not for the exam. Complexity theory defines P and NP on multitape machines and uses the O(t²) simulation to show the classes survive a change of model. Nondeterminism lives on as the certificate idea: a guess plus a short check. SAT solvers walk the same configuration tree with pruning. Search “configuration graph of a nondeterministic Turing machine” and “k-tape to one-tape simulation quadratic overhead”.
